source_text: Quo ergo super naturae iudicio Manichaeus tuque distatis? Quia ille, inquis, malam eam fatetur. Tu ergo si id abnuis, bonam eam esse pronuntia et sublata contentio est; capieris statim veritatis retibus in salutem. Sed reclamas. Audiamus ergo, quid parias, Aristoteles Poenorum. Tantum - inquis - malum ei inest, ut possideatur a diabolo atque aeternum mereatur incendium.
pass_a_gloss: Where therefore over the judgment of nature do the Manichaean and you differ? Because he, you say, confesses it evil. You therefore if you refuse this, pronounce it to be good and the contention is taken away; you will immediately be taken by the nets of truth into salvation. But you reclaim. Let us hear therefore what you bring forth, Aristotle of the Punics. So much evil, you say, is in it, that it is possessed by the devil and deserves eternal fire.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Where, then, do you and Mani differ in your judgment of nature? ‘He admits it is evil,’ you say. If you deny that, then pronounce it good, and the dispute is over. Truth’s nets will immediately catch you for salvation. But you protest. Let us hear what you bring forth, Aristotle of the Carthaginians! ‘So much evil exists within it,’ you say, ‘that the devil possesses it and it deserves eternal fire.’

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
